A1-A2.headline: The Story of the Olympic Games

pages.text: The Olympic Games are huge sports events held around the world. They include Summer Games and Winter Games. Thousands of athletes from more than 200 teams take part in them. These teams represent different countries and territories.
pages.caption: An ice hockey game during the 1928 Winter Olympics at St. Moritz

pages.text: The modern games were inspired by ancient Greek festivals held in Olympia. Baron Pierre de Coubertin started the International Olympic Committee in 1894. This group leads the Olympic movement and makes the rules for the games.
pages.caption: Pierre de Coubertin, co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president

evidence.articleCaption: Pierre de Coubertin, co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president

pages.text: The first modern games took place in Athens in 1896. Later, the games grew very large. Nearly every nation is now represented, and athletes compete for gold, silver, and bronze medals.

Over time, the games expanded to include winter sports like ice hockey and figure skating. A separate Winter Olympics was created. There are also youth games for younger athletes and other special events.
pages.caption: Jesse Owens on the podium after winning the long jump at the 1936 Summer Olympics, where he won four gold medals; in his 1980 obituary, The New York Times called him "perhaps the greatest and most famous athlete in track and field history".

pages.text: Organizing such events brings many challenges, including boycotts, doping, match fixing, bribery, and terrorism. Still, the Olympics and their media exposure provide athletes with the chance to attain national and international fame every two years.

The modern Olympic Games are premier international multi-sport events divided into Summer and Winter editions. They feature thousands of athletes representing over 200 sovereign states and territories, often replacing world championships during their respective years.

pages.text: Inspired by ancient Greek religious and athletic festivals in Olympia, the modern movement was shaped by Baron Pierre de Coubertin. He founded the International Olympic Committee in 1894, which led to the first modern games in Athens in 1896 with support from Greek benefactors.
pages.caption: Pierre de Coubertin, co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president

evidence.articleCaption: Pierre de Coubertin, co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president

pages.text: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries brought major changes. The IOC shifted from pure amateurism to accepting professional athletes. World wars caused cancellations, and political tensions led to boycotts during the Cold War.

To accommodate snow and ice sports, the Winter Olympics were established as a separate event in 1924. After 1992, the Winter and Summer Games were staggered two years apart. The IOC also introduced the Youth Olympic Games and other inclusive sports festivals.

pages.text: Today, nearly every nation participates in the Olympics. While media exposure and commercial sponsorship provide global platforms for athletes and host cities, the movement continues to navigate modern challenges like doping, financial costs, and logistical shifts.

C1-C2.headline: History and Structure of the Olympics

pages.text: The modern Olympic Games constitute a preeminent international multi-sport institution comprising distinct Summer and Winter cycles. Engaging thousands of athletes across more than 200 national delegations, the Games operate under the governance of the International Olympic Committee.
pages.caption: An ice hockey game during the 1928 Winter Olympics at St. Moritz

imageProvenance.credit: Unknown authorUnknown author Unknown authorUnknown author

evidence.articleCaption: An ice hockey game during the 1928 Winter Olympics at St. Moritz

pages.text: Tracing its intellectual lineage to ancient Hellenic festivals in Olympia, the contemporary iteration was catalyzed by Pierre de Coubertin in 1894. Early financial foundations relied heavily on Greek trusts and benefactors to restore the Panathenaic Stadium for the inaugural 1896 Games.
pages.caption: Pierre de Coubertin, co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president

evidence.articleCaption: Pierre de Coubertin, co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president

pages.text: Throughout the twentieth century, the Olympic Movement underwent profound structural transformations. Economic pressures, the abandonment of strict amateurism, and commercialization reshaped participation. Geopolitical conflicts necessitated cancellations during world wars and prominent boycotts during the Cold War era.

Logistical demands prompted the bifurcation of the schedule in 1994, separating the Winter and Summer editions by a two-year interval within each Olympiad. Further diversification manifested through the establishment of the Youth Olympic Games and tailored programs for athletes with disabilities.

pages.text: Representing nearly every sovereign territory today, the Olympic apparatus balances widespread media exposure and national prestige against recurrent controversies such as doping, commercial overreach, and complex financial administration managed through the Olympic Charter.
